literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Chang, under Xiaowen, inherited Marquis of Songzi; by rule the marquisate was demoted to viscount and he was given Baron of Ailing.
idiomatic: His son Chang, under Xiaowen, inherited the Marquisate of Songzi; by rule it was demoted to viscount while he received Baron of Ailing.

literal: Chang was firm and resolute; though there were auspicious celebrations, he never opened his mouth to laugh.
idiomatic: Chang was stern and resolute; even at joyous occasions he never opened his mouth to laugh.

literal: When Xiaowen moved the capital, Chang as Acting Governor remained to garrison and was appointed Grand General of Huaishuo.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen moved the capital, Chang stayed behind as Acting Governor and was appointed Grand General of Huaishuo.

literal: At parting the emperor gave Chang wine; though he bowed and drank, his countenance was not at ease.
idiomatic: At their parting the emperor gave Chang wine; he bowed and drank, yet his face showed no ease.

literal: The emperor said, "I hear you have never laughed in your life; now we are separated by mountains—you should laugh for Us."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "They say you have never laughed in all your life; now mountains lie between us—you ought to laugh for me."

literal: In the end he could not.
idiomatic: He still could not.

literal: The emperor said, "The qi of the Five Phases—some places it does not enter;
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The qi of the Five Phases—surely it does not enter every place alike;

literal: between the Six Directions, what affair could there not be!"
idiomatic: between the Six Directions, what could not happen!"

literal: Those present on left and right all clutched their wrists and laughed greatly.
idiomatic: Those standing by all clutched their wrists and burst out laughing.

literal: Under Xuanwu he was Northern Central Commander and concurrently Governor of Henei.
idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he served as Northern Central Commander with concurrent appointment as Governor of Henei.

literal: Chang, because the Heqiao bridge cables made the road narrow and inconvenient for travelers, and autumn floods each year destroyed it, therefore made a boat route.
idiomatic: Finding the Heqiao bridge cables too narrow for travelers and the autumn floods destroying it yearly, Chang built a boat route instead.

literal: He then broadly recruited empty carts leaving the capital and ordered each to haul one pair of stones, piling them to form banks.
idiomatic: He recruited empty carts leaving the capital and ordered each to haul one pair of stones, piling them into embankments.

literal: The bridge widened and coming and going were convenient.
idiomatic: The crossing widened and travel became easy.

literal: The commanderies near the bridge were no longer troubled; public and private alike relied on it.
idiomatic: Nearby commanderies were spared further hardship; public and private interests alike benefited.

literal: He successively held Director of Revenue, Palace Attendant, and Governor of Yong Province.
idiomatic: He later served as Director of Revenue, Palace Attendant, and Governor of Yong Province.

literal: He died; posthumous name Cheng.
idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Cheng.

literal: After midlife his office was only modestly advanced; he then became self-important and arrogant, without ritual within the inner quarters, discord among brothers, and by nature greedy and cruel—commentators despised him.
idiomatic: In midlife his offices rose only modestly; he grew arrogant, neglected ritual at home, quarreled with his brothers, and was greedy and cruel—commentators despised him.

literal: Chang's son Zihua, style Furong, inherited the title.
idiomatic: Chang's son Zihua, style Furong, inherited the title.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he was appointed Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: At the start of Xiaozhuang he was made Governor of Qi Province.

literal: Before this the province had several times suffered rebellion; in Xing Gao's disorder the people could not protect themselves.
idiomatic: The province had repeatedly suffered rebellion; during Xing Gao's uprising the people could not protect themselves.

literal: Zihua gathered and settled the powerful families, entrusting them with keys and bolts; all were moved and pleased, and within the borders there was calm.
idiomatic: Zihua gathered the local magnates, entrusted them with authority, won their loyalty, and brought the region to calm.

literal: But his nature was very narrow and urgent; when urgent he did not choose his words and with his own hands would strike and beat.
idiomatic: Yet he was narrow and hot-tempered; in a rage he spoke without restraint and struck people with his own hands.

literal: Chief Clerk Zheng Zizhan was Zihua's close friend.
idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zheng Zizhan was his close friend.

literal: Seeing insult and abuse, he immediately left.
idiomatic: After being insulted and abused, Zizhan left at once.

literal: Though Zihua afterward reproached himself sternly, in the end he could not change.
idiomatic: Zihua later reproached himself, but in the end he could not change.

literal: In office he did not perform hypocritical conduct; whenever there were gifts, he mostly declined much and accepted little—therefore people did not resent his taking.
idiomatic: He did not put on false rectitude in office; when offered gifts he usually declined most and accepted little, so people did not resent him.

literal: In judging cases and interrogating prisoners he strove for benevolence and forbearance; the people of Qi erected a stele praising his virtue.
idiomatic: In trials he favored mercy and forbearance; the people of Qi raised a stele praising his virtue.

literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Ji Province.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, the people of Qi Province expelled the governor Zhao Luozhou; Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan memorialized Fang Shida of Jinan as acting governor.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Qi Province expelled its governor Zhao Luozhou; Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan had Fang Shida of Jinan act as governor.

literal: Luozhou's son Yuanyian had earlier followed Zihua in Ji Province; he intercepted the messenger, altered the memorial, and asked that Zihua be restored as Governor of Ji.
idiomatic: Luozhou's son Yuanyian, who had served under Zihua in Ji, intercepted the dispatch, altered the memorial, and asked that Zihua be restored as governor.

literal: Zihua's mother the Lady Fang once went to a relative's for food and drink; returning at night she vomited greatly, and people thought she had been poisoned—his mother was very fearful.
idiomatic: Zihua's mother Lady Fang once dined with kin; returning at night she vomited violently, and people suspected poison—she was terrified.

literal: Zihua thereupon scooped up the vomit and ate it all; his mother then was at ease.
idiomatic: Zihua scooped up the vomit and ate it; only then did his mother grow calm.

literal: Soon because of mourning for his mother he returned to the capital.
idiomatic: Soon he returned to the capital to mourn his mother.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he was appointed Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
idiomatic: At the start of Xiaojing he was made Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

literal: His younger brother Zisi was sent on mission to the Pass west; the court sent Right Guards General Guo Qiong to seize him.
idiomatic: His younger brother Zisi was sent on mission west of the Pass; the court sent Right Guards General Guo Qiong to arrest him.

literal: Zisi said to Guo's servant, "Quickly kill me—why long detain a man of the state?"
idiomatic: Zisi told Guo's attendant, "Kill me at once—why hold a servant of the realm so long?"

literal: Zihua said to Zisi, "Because of your carelessness you have brought me to this!"
idiomatic: Zihua said to Zisi, "Your carelessness has brought me to this!"

literal: He knocked his head on the bed, weeping beyond control.
idiomatic: He beat his head on the bed and wept beyond control.

literal: Zisi stroked his beard with his hand, turned to Zihua and said, "Sir, your constitution is ill."
idiomatic: Zisi stroked his beard and told Zihua, "Sir, your constitution is unwell."

literal: Soon he and Zisi were both granted death at the Outer Office below the Gate.
idiomatic: Soon both brothers were ordered to die at the Outer Office below the Gate.

literal: Zisi, style Zhongnian, was by nature fierce and violent and always prided himself on loyalty and valor.
idiomatic: Zisi, style Zhongnian, was fierce and violent and always prided himself on loyalty and valor.

literal: When Yuan Tianmu held court power, through kinship he recommended him as Imperial Censor.
idiomatic: When Yuan Tianmu held court power he recommended Zisi, as a kinsman, for Imperial Censor.

literal: Before this, Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shun memorialized that the Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices; as to public affairs, they ought not be sent to the censor.
idiomatic: Earlier, Concurrent Vice Director Yuan Shun had argued that the Masters of Writing are the root of government and their public business should not be routed to the censor.

literal: When it came to Zisi, he memorialized:
idiomatic: Zisi now memorialized:

literal: Examining the Censor's Ordinance: "The censor supervises the hundred offices; the attendant censor investigates the inner palace."
idiomatic: He cited the Censor's Ordinance: "The censor supervises the hundred offices; the attendant censor investigates the inner palace."

literal: It also says, "When the censor goes out, carriage hubs go before him, clearing the road for one li; dukes, marquises, and the hundred offices avoid the road."
idiomatic: It also states that when the censor goes abroad his escort clears the road for one li and nobles and officials must yield.

literal: Through four emperors, some twenty censors before and after all followed this in their rounds and never for a moment abolished it; prefectures, directorates, and ministries all followed this ordinance.
idiomatic: Across four reigns some twenty censors had followed this practice without interruption; every ministry observed the same rule.

literal: Only in Emperor Suzong's time, mourning for Lin Tao, did Concurrent Left Vice Director Shun refuse to give his name and also refused to send the register.
idiomatic: Only under Emperor Suzong, during mourning for Lin Tao, had Vice Director Shun refused both to register his name and to send the roster.

literal: The former censor Li Daoyuan reported and memorialized; Shun again replied, "The Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices; directors and vice directors are noble in receiving words—they should not be subordinated to the censor or have names sent to the censor."
idiomatic: Former censor Li Daoyuan had reported this; Shun replied that directors of the Masters of Writing were too exalted to be subordinated to the censor or listed on his roster.

literal: Soon an edict also permitted it as he memorialized.
idiomatic: An edict soon permitted Shun's request.

literal: From then until now there has been no single standard.
idiomatic: Since then there has been no uniform standard.

literal: When I first entered the bureau I clearly saw this affair and wished to request a ruling, but because power was divided I did not dare act at once.
idiomatic: When I first took office I saw this clearly and wished to press for a ruling, but with power divided I dared not act immediately.

literal: Day after day it passed through heat and cold.
idiomatic: Day after day the matter dragged on.

literal: On the first of last month the bureau sent to the Masters of Writing requesting the roster of those who should attend court, but the ministry detained it and would not send.
idiomatic: On the first of last month the bureau requested the court-attendance roster from the Masters of Writing, but the ministry withheld it.

literal: Soon it sent another urgent demand to the chief clerks; suddenly Attendant Lang Pei Xianbo appended a note: "According to old precedent, when the censor meets a bureau lang in the covered passage the censor descends and holds his tablet while the lang raises his hand in salute from the carriage—thus they are clearly not equals."
idiomatic: A renewed demand went to the chief clerks; then Attendant Lang Pei Xianbo appended a note citing old precedent that the censor saluted a bureau lang from the carriage step—proof, he said, that they were not equals.

literal: Seeing this I was deeply astonished; pondering it two or three times I did not understand the reason.
idiomatic: I was astonished; pondering it repeatedly I could not understand their reasoning.

literal: I thought the capital ministry had separately received a new form, altering Gaozu's old command; I sent to ask on what authority.
idiomatic: I thought the capital ministry had adopted some new form overturning Gaozu's command and asked on what authority.

literal: I also received Attendant Lang Wang Yuanxu's reply: "From Cai's Han Offices—it seems not forced."
idiomatic: Attendant Lang Wang Yuanxu replied that the citation came from Cai's Han Offices and was not far-fetched.

literal: Then I knew Pei and Wang also wished to break the canonical statutes; both men's hearts sought self-justification.
idiomatic: Then I knew Pei and Wang meant to overturn established law; both sought only to justify themselves.

literal: I examine the Biography of Xuan Bing in the Han History: an edict summoned Bing as Imperial Censor, and he with the Director of Justice and Director of the Masters of Writing all met in the palace hall, each with a separate seat—they were called in the capital the Three Solitary Seats.
idiomatic: The Han History's biography of Xuan Bing records that censor, director of justice, and director of the Masters of Writing each had a separate seat in the hall—the Three Solitary Seats of the capital.

literal: I also find in the Wei History biography of Cui Yan and the Jin Wenyang biography of Fu Gu—all say that once one is censor the hundred offices tremble in fear.
idiomatic: The Wei History's Cui Yan and Jin's Fu Gu likewise say that once one becomes censor the hundred offices tremble.

literal: From this, that the censor does not bow to ministry langs has been so for long.
idiomatic: Thus the censor's not bowing to ministry langs is an ancient practice.

literal: That the Censorate does not belong to the capital seat is also not of today.
idiomatic: That the Censorate stands apart from the capital directorate is likewise nothing new.

literal: I further find in the Duty Ordinance: "If one is late to court assembly, he is impeached."
idiomatic: The Duty Ordinance also states that lateness to court is impeachable.

literal: Then the registers of the hundred offices ought to be sent up to the bureau—this is plainly clear.
idiomatic: Therefore the roster of the hundred offices must be sent to the bureau—plainly so.

literal: Also the crown prince and below, if they violate the statutes, may all be investigated—then directors and vice directors' court names ought to be delivered to the censor; this too is manifest.
idiomatic: Since even the crown prince may be investigated for violations, directors' names belong on the censor's roster—equally manifest.

literal: If names are not delivered, by what proof are good and ill judged?
idiomatic: Without the roster, how is merit or fault to be judged?

literal: Shun's stubborn holding was not fair and penetrating;
idiomatic: Shun's stubborn insistence was neither fair nor reasonable;

literal: the former dynasty's indulgence—how was that correct law!
idiomatic: the former dynasty's indulgence was hardly correct law!

literal: I respectfully report Attendant Lang Pei Xianbo, Wang Yuanxu, and others—men who stand among the scholar stream and long served in pure office—lightly playing with brief notes, brilliant thus; if they cling to heterodox views, suddenly it comes to this.
idiomatic: I report Attendant Langs Pei Xianbo and Wang Yuanxu—men of standing who toyed with brief notes until heterodoxy reached this pass.

literal: If this is not disciplined, court ordinances will be ruined.
idiomatic: If this goes unpunished, court ordinances will collapse.

literal: I ask that according to the present case Xianbo and others be removed from their posts and handed to the law office.
idiomatic: I ask that Xianbo and the rest be removed from office and handed to the law office.

literal: The Masters of Writing are the root of receiving words; directors and vice directors are the pivot of the hundred offices—like floating vanity they assist this deviation; the chief offenders should be clearly identified and their crimes graded by degree.
idiomatic: Directors of the Masters of Writing are chiefs of government; aiding this deviation they should be chief offenders, punished by degree.

literal: The edict said, "States differ in government—ancient affairs cannot be relied on."
idiomatic: The edict said, "States differ in government—ancient precedent cannot govern us."

literal: Hand it to the office to examine Gaozu's old rules and report gains and losses.
idiomatic: Let the office examine Gaozu's old rules and report what should stand or fall.

literal: Soon following Zisi's memorial, he again incurred Yuan Tianmu's resentment and was stopped.
idiomatic: Soon after Zisi's memorial he again angered Yuan Tianmu and was removed.

literal: When Yuan Hao was defeated he was enfeoffed Viscount of Anding.
idiomatic: After Yuan Hao's defeat he was enfeoffed Viscount of Anding.

literal: Under Xiaojing he held Palace Attendant and died.
idiomatic: Under Xiaojing he served as Palace Attendant and died.

literal: Chang's younger brother Zhen, style Jinque, inherited Baron of Ailing.
idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Zhen, style Jinque, inherited Baron of Ailing.

literal: Under Xuanwu he curried favor with Gao Zhao and thereby won the emperor's intimacy.
idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he curried favor with Gao Zhao and won the emperor's intimacy.

literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led stalwarts and killed him.
idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led bravos who killed him.

literal: Later he died in the post of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He later died as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Ping's younger brother Changsheng held the post of Mobile Cavalry General and died.
idiomatic: Ping's younger brother Changsheng served as Mobile Cavalry General and died.

literal: Under Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu was exalted, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Under Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu rose high, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

literal: Tianmu was by nature mild and generous, handsome in appearance, and famous for archery.
idiomatic: Tianmu was mild and generous, handsome, and famed for archery.

literal: In the disorder of the Six Garrisons, Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong and Prince of Guangyang Shen campaigned north; Tianmu as Grand Preceptor was sent to comfort the armies.
idiomatic: During the Six Garrisons uprising, Li Chong and Prince of Guangyang Shen marched north while Tianmu, as Grand Preceptor, was sent to comfort the troops.

literal: Passing Xiurong he met Erzhu Rong, deeply bound themselves, and pledged brotherhood.
idiomatic: Passing Xiurong he met Erzhu Rong; they bound themselves closely and swore brotherhood.

literal: Before long he was reassigned a separate commander, went to Xiurong, became Rong's trusted core, and was appointed Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Soon reassigned as a separate commander, he went to Xiurong, became Rong's intimate, and was made Governor of Bing Province.

literal: When Rong went to Luoyang, Tianmu took part in the opening plot.
idiomatic: When Rong marched on Luoyang, Tianmu shared in the opening plot.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang succeeded, he was appointed Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang, and summoned to the capital.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne Tianmu was made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shangdang and summoned to the capital.

literal: Later his fief was increased, totaling thirty thousand households in all.
idiomatic: His fief was later increased to thirty thousand households in all.

literal: Soon he supervised the national history, recorded the Masters of Writing, opened a bureau, and hereditarily held Bing Province.
idiomatic: He soon supervised the national history, recorded the Masters of Writing, opened a bureau, and held Bing Province by hereditary right.

literal: At first Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli were bandits; the people of Ying and Ji provinces mostly fled south to escape disorder.
idiomatic: At first Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli raided; people of Ying and Ji fled south.

literal: Hejian Xing Gao of the former Beiping prefecture led his followers, encamped at Mao city to resist Luozhou and Ge Rong, nearly three years.
idiomatic: Xing Gao of Hejian led his band, held Mao city against Luozhou and Ge Rong for nearly three years.

literal: After Prince of Guangyang Shen and others were defeated, Gao crossed south and dwelt on the border of Qingzhou and Beihai.
idiomatic: After Shen's defeat Gao crossed south to the Qingzhou–Beihai border.

literal: Empress Ling ordered that wherever displaced people were found they be placed, assigned to commanderies and counties, and powerful locals chosen as magistrates to soothe them.
idiomatic: Empress Ling ordered displaced people settled under local magistrates chosen from powerful families.

literal: At the time Governor of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun memorialized to establish Xin'an commandery with Gao as governor; no reply came.
idiomatic: Governor of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun asked to establish Xin'an with Gao as governor; no reply came.

literal: When the court streamlined appointments to commanderies and counties, because Gao's nephew Ziyao's hereditary qualification ranked ahead, he was instead given Hejian as governor.
idiomatic: When the court streamlined county appointments, Gao's nephew Ziyao's hereditary rank placed him ahead, and Gao was passed over for Hejian.

literal: Gao was deeply shamed and resentful, and thereupon rebelled.
idiomatic: Deeply shamed, Gao rebelled.
